issues.existing: horned mask with two curved horns and dark eye openings
issues.observed: the eye openings are pale and luminous, not dark
issues.evidence: Both eye apertures read as bright bluish-white shapes against the near-black mask face — they are among the lighter values in that region of the frame and are the reason the mask reads as the visual centre. 'Dark eye openings' inverts the tonal fact.

issues.existing: the two figures face inward toward the central mask, framing it symmetrically
issues.observed: both figures are seen from behind with their bodies turned away from the viewer, not turned to face the mask
issues.evidence: The left figure presents a full back view — shoulder blades, spine line and the rear of the head — with both arms raised overhead; his body axis points away from the viewer, not toward the plinth. The right figure is likewise seen from behind, with only her head angled slightly to her left. Neither torso is rotated toward the centre, so 'face inward toward the central mask' is not what is painted.

issues.existing: the chain arcs from the left figure's raised hands across the upper left of the frame
issues.observed: the chain stays within the figure's own silhouette — a loop between his raised hands just above his head, then draping down his back and left hip
issues.evidence: The upper left of the frame is open star field with a large crescent-lit sphere in it and no chain crossing it. The chain is visible only as the loop spanning his two raised hands immediately above the head, and as links running down across the shoulder, back and hip.

issues.existing: the two figures face inward toward the central mask, framing it symmetrically

issues.evidence: The left figure's arms are raised overhead and his head is tipped back and up at the starfield — his attention is upward, not at the plinth. He also stands markedly closer to the viewer and renders much larger than the right figure, so the pair does not frame the mask symmetrically.
